recommendations.rationale: A defer executes nothing: no candidate is built, no backend solve is consumed and the single execution allowance remains unused. A passing terminal reach (terminal_error_m 0.00764 m inside the 0.01 m limit) coexists with a failing sampled holding on speed (late-window motion far above the 0.02 m/s limit over 0.05 s), while computation records show ~15-30 s solves against a 0.01 s period, 35 deadline misses and initialization-dominated plan selection; a single execution without closed-loop counterfactual replay cannot isolate a dominant cause, and controller weights, materials and geometry are outside this phase's authorization, so no parameter value is proposed.

A saved-state comparison (one-step predicted endpoint versus backend endpoint at matched timestamps) plus a repeated identical replay would test the projected-model-divergence and run-variation hypotheses. No numerical check is authorized in this phase, so this remains deferred and no projected model effect is claimed here.

Locating the update at which tip speed stopped decreasing requires per-update warm plans and optimizer iteration traces, which are not retained (source.historical_full_plans retained=false; full_snapshots_available false). Deferred until such retention exists.

attribution.reason: Reach and holding evaluate different quantities on the same run: the reach verdict uses terminal position error 0.00764 m inside the 0.01 m limit, whereas sampled holding is judged jointly on position and speed over a 0.05 s window and fails with late_max_error_m 0.0581 m and residual terminal speed 0.6352 m/s (handed-over late_max_speed_m_s 1.5810152739742807 m/s is about 79x the 0.02 m/s limit, stated as prose from supplied feedback since it has no handle here). The retained records do not localize which update left the tip moving or why braking did not complete.

Recorded per-update solves of about 15-30 s against a 0.01 s control period, 35 deadline misses and a stopping-count profile dominated by User_Requested_Stop (34) with one Solve_Succeeded are consistent with inputs being reused rather than recomputed at each 10 ms step. This is one execution without closed-loop counterfactual replay, so it is a candidate relationship, not an established dominant cause.

initialization_selected 29 of 35 recorded updates, shortened effective horizons (9 and 2 control intervals in the sampled updates) and accepted plans carrying nonzero returned_constraint_violation are consistent with selection being dominated by warm-start/initialization reuse. Historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained, so the update at which tip speed stopped decreasing cannot be located.

reach_passed is true with terminal_error_m 0.007642608585867386 m below the 0.01 m limit, so a reach-tolerance violation is not the failing criterion; this says nothing about the separate holding-window failure.

The retained comparisons are matched next-timestamp, single-step projected-versus-backend endpoint checks with explicitly recorded scope and some intervals whose projected state was unavailable; a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot account for the whole 0.05 s holding window, and no causal-identification or closed-loop replay capability is retained.

No retained record in this context links any geometry or material variable to the holding-window speed excursion, and the improvement phase selected no change (defer with empty changes), so nothing here supports a geometry delta; equally, nothing here rules geometry out.

facts.statement: Baseline execution 4e358bd36ab54be3afd5003f36ff8110 records reach_passed true with terminal_error_m 0.007642608585867386 m, inside the 0.01 m settling position limit, while terminal_speed_m_s is 0.6351726092425104 m/s, far above the 0.02 m/s speed limit; the reach verdict is therefore decided on terminal position, not on residual motion.

On the same execution, sampled_settling_passed is false with late_max_error_m 0.05813810428573256 m against the 0.01 m position limit over the 0.05 s window; the displayed final-window sample detail.late_motion[0].error_m equals that same 0.05813810428573256 m, and a displayed late-window sample speed is 0.7758084264853817 m/s against the 0.02 m/s limit.

Computation records for this execution: mean_update_s 17.303696897140306 s against control_period_s 0.01 s, deadline_misses 35, stopping_counts.Solve_Succeeded 1, initialization_selected 29 of total_updates 35; sampled solver times include optimization_solve_s 15.225156700005755 s (update 0) and 15.611759999999776 s (update 20) with update_wall_s 29.732597999973223 s (update 0).

Sampled per-update records show effective_horizon 9 (update 26) and 2 (update 33) control intervals, an accepted plan carrying returned_constraint_violation 0.012896929259021382 (update 26), projection_residual_rad_m values 0.7770172782654128 (update 10), 1.8265102189800908 (update 20), 2.347088656497748 (update 26) and 2.3741307545542503 (update 34), and matched single-step comparisons whose recorded scope is 'Matched next timestamp and applied input; projected GVS prediction versus full serial-backend endpoint, not full state agreement', with one interval noting 'next projected state unavailable; endpoint comparison remains available'.

This revision context records the improvement phase as a defer with empty changes and no executed candidate, so no post-change profile measurements exist to compare with the baseline; retained capabilities flag causal_identification as unsupported, record full_snapshots_available false, and state that single execution and model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause.

limitations: Single execution: the retained records support only candidate relationships, not a dominant cause; model comparisons and handed-over summaries do not establish causality.

No candidate executed: the improvement phase recorded a defer with empty changes, so there is no post-change profile result to compare against the baseline; adopting a recommendation would execute nothing.

Sampled backend motion in this context is partial (queried samples are listed in the missing-evidence entries); there is no continuous-time reconstruction, so the onset of the position/speed excursion inside the holding window is not localized.
Historical full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces (control_snapshots.json) are not retained, so per-iteration cost behaviour is not reconstructable.

Several request figures have no fact_catalog handle in this context and are reported as prose from handed-over content only: late_max_speed_m_s 1.5810152739742807 m/s, noninitialization_selected 6, max_cpu_s 30.0, configured horizon 10, holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0 and terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0.
Recorded cost weights (tracking 1.0, terminal 5.0, velocity/variation/tension 1e-4 to 1e-3) do not establish which term dominated without actual contributions.

No closed-loop counterfactual replay, causal-attribution tool, or full-backend replay exists, and controller-parameter, geometry and material changes are outside this phase's authorization, so the computation-versus-holding relationship cannot be tested here.
recommended_actions: Defer any controller-parameter or geometry change: a single execution without counterfactual replay cannot support one, no retained record links geometry or material variables to the holding-window speed excursion, and the defer decision executed nothing.

If a later grant allows, characterize the projected-model divergence using the recorded saved-state comparison (one-step predicted endpoint versus backend endpoint at matched timestamps) plus a repeated identical replay to separate run-to-run variation from a systematic pattern.
If a later grant allows, retain full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces so the update at which tip speed stopped decreasing can be located.

If a change is later authorized, controller-side hypotheses to examine are tip-speed weighting in the holding/terminal cost and the solver-return/effective-horizon budget (effective horizons 9 and 2 recorded); these are hypotheses to test, not executed actions.

decision.expected_measurable_effect: None: a defer executes nothing, so no geometry candidate is built, no backend solve is consumed, and the single execution allowance remains unused. Reach: no expected change - terminal_error_m stays at the recorded 0.00764 m, already inside the 0.01 m position limit. Sampled holding: no expected change - the failing speed criterion (late-window maximum 1.5810 m/s versus the 0.02 m/s limit over the 0.05 s window) is untouched by any granted geometry value, and no granted variable is linked by retained evidence to that excursion. Computation: no expected change - mean_update_s 17.303696897140306 s versus control_period_s 0.01 s, deadline_misses 35 and the User_Requested_Stop-dominated solver statuses are unaffected by arm length or section scale. Uncertainty: if a change were later authorized under an expanded grant, the sign and magnitude of its effect on any of these three quantities cannot be predicted from the retained records, and no derived numerical projection is offered here.
decision.rationale: The accepted diagnosis (report 3de90be9..., execution 4e358bd36ab54be3afd5003f36ff8110) leaves every candidate relationship at "possible"/"insufficient_evidence" and rules out only a reach-tolerance violation: reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m 0.00764 m inside the 0.01 m limit, while sampled holding fails on speed - late-window maximum speed 1.5810 m/s against the 0.02 m/s limit over the 0.05 s window, with residual terminal speed 0.6352 m/s. The observations aligned with the failing criterion are computational and controller-side: mean_update_s 17.303696897140306 s against control_period_s 0.01 s, deadline_misses 35, stopping_counts User_Requested_Stop 34 versus Solve_Succeeded 1, initialization_selected 29 of 35 updates, and sampled effective_horizon values of 9 and 2 against a configured horizon of 10. The only recipe terms that would directly target tip-speed damping (holding and terminal tip-speed weights, recorded as 0.0) are controller parameters, and controller weights, materials, force limits and task changes are not authorized in this phase. No retained record ties components/near/length_m, components/far/length_m, design/section_scale or design/material_scenario to the holding-window speed excursion, and historical full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained (source.historical_full_plans retained=false). A single execution without closed-loop counterfactual replay cannot separate run-to-run variation from a systematic effect, so proposing a geometry delta solely to spend the one permitted candidate build would be an unsupported change; the intent is deferred with empty changes, and the specific unsupported future work is controller-side (tip-speed weighting in the holding/terminal cost, solver-return and effective-horizon budget) rather than geometry.
